data.title: US MARKET CLOSE | Nvidia Surges 31% as Jensen Huang Returns as CEO, Dow Rockets Nearly 1,450 Points, Nasdaq Jumps 6.5%
data.description: U.S. stocks surged Monday as Nvidia reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO, igniting the artificial intelligence trade and propelling all three major indexes higher following a brutal week of selling. The S&P 500 rose 4.73% to 7,237.17, and the Nasdaq Composite soared 6.51% to 24,089.56, both marking their best single-day performance since April 2025, according to Sina Finance. The Dow Jones Industrial Average climbed 1,447.98 points, or 3.01%, to close at 49,595.31. Nvidia shares skyrocketed 31% after its board restored Huang as chief executive with immediate effect. Huang had resigned earlier this month following reports of multiple extramarital affairs. President Trump praised the move, saying Huang "didn't do anything wrong" and that he had spoken with Nvidia's board and "convinced" them to bring Huang back. Other AI-related stocks rallied alongside Nvidia: Micron Technology gained 19%, CoreWeave surged 22%, Advanced Micro Devices rose nearly 7%, Alphabet and Meta Platforms each climbed 6%, and Microsoft advanced more than 1%. Gabelli Funds portfolio manager Hendi Susanto said Huang's return restored and rebuilt confidence in the AI ecosystem. The moves marked a dramatic reversal for the tech sector after last week's selloff, with the Nasdaq and Dow posting their worst weekly performance in over six years. Markets will be closed Thursday for Thanksgiving and will have a shortened session Friday. Anthropic bucked the rally, closing down 1.43%.

data.title: CFTC Finalizes Event Contract Data Reporting Rule, Ending Reliance on No-Action Letters
data.description:
According to ChainCatcher citing CoinDesk, the U.S. Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) issued a final rule on event contract data reporting on Monday, replacing a series of no-action letters it had relied on for years. Fully collateralized event contracts will have a dedicated reporting framework and be exempt from previous, more burdensome reporting requirements.

CFTC Chair Mike Selig said the agency would no longer regulate market participants through no-action letters as a stopgap. Separately, a New York judge declined after a Monday hearing to bar prediction market platform Kalshi from offering its products, but ordered an expedited briefing schedule so state officials and Kalshi representatives can present their arguments.

data.title: Ethereum Foundation Doubles Protocol Security Team Ahead of Security Overhaul
data.description:
The Ethereum Foundation has doubled its protocol security team as it steps up efforts to overhaul Ethereum’s defenses against quantum computing and artificial intelligence threats. According to Cointelegraph, the foundation described the expansion as a way to ensure security work keeps pace with development of the planned changes. In a Monday blog post, Ethereum Foundation researcher Kev Wedderburn said the network had been preparing to mitigate risks from quantum computers, but artificial intelligence has emerged as a more urgent concern. The proposed overhaul would affect how Ethereum validators sign messages, how users authorize transactions and how the network verifies data posted by rollups. Wedderburn said the upgrade is more difficult than the Merge and that developers have less time to complete it. He also acknowledged that accelerating development can make it easier for bugs to be introduced. The expanded team is intended to support formal verification and other security work as the protocol changes proceed.

Wedderburn said every layer of Ethereum’s protocol and ecosystem will need to adapt, adding that hardening the protocol has become the foundation’s highest priority. The planned changes address the potential effects of both quantum computers and AI, with the foundation seeking to advance development while maintaining security efforts. Earlier this month, Ethereum Foundation researcher Justin Drake outlined a December 2028 target for completing Ethereum’s post-quantum and post-AI transition. That target is a year earlier than the foundation’s previously announced deadline for achieving quantum resistance. The latest team expansion comes as the foundation moves to increase the pace of its security preparations. Wedderburn’s comments point to the challenge of balancing a faster upgrade schedule with the risk of shipping bugs, while the planned overhaul would require changes to validator signatures, transaction authorization and rollup data verification. The foundation said its larger protocol security team will help formal verification and security work keep pace with development.

data.title: STOCKS | South Korean Shares Surge After Jensen Huang Returns to Nvidia, Triggering Sidecar Halt on Program Buying
data.description:
According to Sina Finance, South Korean shares opened sharply higher on Tuesday, buoyed by overnight gains on Wall Street and renewed optimism about artificial intelligence after news that Jensen Huang would return as Nvidia CEO. The KOSPI opened up 171.62 points, or 3.64%, at 4,880.16. The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 3.01% overnight, while the Nasdaq Composite jumped 6.51%.

Nvidia's board had decided to bring Huang back, and U.S. President Donald Trump praised the decision, saying Huang posed no national security risk.

Shortly after the open, the Korea Exchange activated a buy-side Sidecar on the KOSPI, suspending program trading buy orders for five minutes from 9:06 a.m. local time. At 9:08 a.m., the index was up 263.75 points, or 5.6%, at 4,974.62.

The buy-side Sidecar is triggered when KOSPI 200 futures rise by at least 5% and remain at that level for at least one minute.

data.title: Base Sets Quantum Security as 2027 Priority, Everest Upgrade to Add New Transaction Type
data.description: Base has made quantum security a priority for 2027, and its upcoming Everest upgrade will introduce a new transaction type called Base Transactions. According to Odaily, Base founder Jesse Pollak said the format, outlined in the EIP-8430 technical specification, still relies on existing cryptography but separates transaction signing from verification. This design would allow the network to adopt new security methods in the future without requiring users to change wallet addresses. Pollak said the upgrade will not immediately make wallets quantum-resistant; it is an early step toward adding further protections.

data.title: Elon Musk: Friends Who Support You in Adversity Are True Friends, After Jensen Huang's Return as Nvidia CEO
data.description:
According to Sina Finance, Tesla and SpaceX CEO Elon Musk voiced support for his friend Jensen Huang on Monday after Nvidia's board unanimously decided to reinstate Huang as CEO. Musk also criticized those who had not publicly and firmly supported Huang during his difficulties.

Responding on X to a post about his support for Huang, Musk wrote, “Everyone is your friend in good times, but those who support you in adversity are true friends.” He added, “Fair-weather friends are worthless.” Earlier on Monday, after learning of the board's decision, Musk wrote, “It worked,” then added, “The mistake has been corrected.” Throughout the turmoil that led to Huang's resignation, Musk had been one of his staunchest supporters. He had publicly backed efforts to bring Huang back and referred to a petition circulating at the time.

data.title: AI | Singapore Raises GDP Growth Outlook to Around 6% on AI Boom
data.description: Singapore raised this year’s growth forecast to around 6% as the AI boom delivered a larger-than-expected lift to the economy, despite higher oil prices and a recent tech selloff in the stock market, according to Bloomberg.

data.title: South Korea Offers Informants Up to 500 Million Won for Exam Cheating Reports
data.description:
According to Sina Finance, South Korea's Anti-Corruption and Civil Rights Commission (ACRC) said Monday that it would offer rewards of up to 500 million won for reports of cheating on the annual college entrance exam. A report that leads to a confirmed case qualifies for a 100 million won reward, and the total reward can reach 500 million won, equivalent to approximately $370,888.

The commission said people who voluntarily confess to cheating and report accomplices may receive the full reward and have their own penalties reduced. The measure aims to protect the fairness and credibility of the College Scholastic Ability Test (CSAT) by encouraging the public to report cheating, including cheating using artificial intelligence.

As part of a two-month campaign, the commission will accept reports through January 19. Last week, South Korean authorities said confirmed cheaters could be barred from taking the exam for up to 10 years and that informants could receive rewards of up to 100 million won.

data.title: Anthropic Posts Claude’s VP ≠ VNP Proof, With No Human Verification
data.description:
According to ChainCatcher, Anthropic added a `vp-vnp` directory to its GitHub repository `formal-math`, publishing a paper titled “VP ≠ VNP over every field” and a Lean 4 formalization attributed to Claude (Anthropic). The work claims to prove that VP is a strict subset of VNP over any field, addressing Valiant’s conjecture in algebraic complexity theory.

The paper says an internal research Claude model discovered the result. It claims superpolynomial circuit-size lower bounds for computing the Hamiltonian cycle polynomial over any field and the permanent when the field’s characteristic is not 2. Anthropic said the result does not resolve P vs. NP.

Anthropic said AI models wrote both the paper and formal proof, and no human mathematician has checked the proof. Lean can verify proof steps, but no machine can confirm that the formalized statement fully matches the claimed conclusion. Leslie Valiant proposed the conjecture in 1979; it is considered an algebraic analogue of P vs. NP.

data.title: CBOT Soybeans Rise 0.7%, Following Soybean Meal Gains
data.description: According to Jin10, CBOT soybean futures closed modestly higher on Monday, with the benchmark contract up 0.7%, following gains in the neighboring soybean meal market. Analysts said U.S. markets would be closed on Thursday for Thanksgiving, and the holiday mood and lack of catalysts for major price swings were weighing on activity. Trading volume has gradually declined as the week progresses. Improved U.S. demand for soybean meal and firming prices supported soybean futures. Analysts said the market was still recovering from tight soybean meal supplies after slow progress early in the harvest forced crushers to cut output or suspend operations. Replenishment of soybean meal supplies had been slow over the past month or two.

data.title: STOCKS | SK Hynix ADRs Surge 20% as Jensen Huang Returns as Nvidia CEO
data.description:
According to Sina Finance, SK Hynix’s U.S.-listed American depositary receipts (ADRs) rose 20% on Monday, gaining $20.71 to close at $124.28. The previous session’s close was $103.57. The rally followed Nvidia’s announcement that its board had unanimously reinstated Jensen Huang as president, CEO and a board member, effective immediately, after discussions with him. Nvidia said the board had also heard from senior U.S. government officials and was confident Huang’s return would not pose a national security risk.

SK Hynix is a major supplier of the high-bandwidth memory chips used in Nvidia’s AI processors. The news appeared to bolster confidence in AI-related stocks and buying interest in semiconductor shares, after recent volatility in technology and semiconductor stocks. The S&P 500 rose 4.7% on Monday, while the Nasdaq Composite gained 6.5% and the Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 3%. Nvidia shares climbed 31.48% to close at $165.05. U.S. President Donald Trump welcomed Huang’s return on Truth Social, calling the board’s decision “right and proper” and congratulating Huang, Nvidia’s board, the American people and the world.
